hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 1->3 carries no signal and adds little.
Edge 1->2 is fed only through node 1, which is disconnected when edge 0 is none, so the conv is wasted.
Replacing none with a skip adds a direct input-to-output path (a gain), whereas replacing a conv with a skip is a loss.
Replacing a strong conv on the direct edge with a skip loses representational power.
Removing a 3x3 conv on the first edge costs far more than removing a weak op.
Deleting a conv edge hurts more than deleting a pool or skip edge.
Adding a conv where there was no edge opens a new learnable path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 4 removed, the conv on edge 0 only reaches the output via node 2, so its benefit is reduced.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to 1x1 loses accuracy, unlike replacing a weak op.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 gets input only through node 1, so the conv on edge 5 has less useful signal to process.
